memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"The nations will hear and tremble; anguish will grip the people of Philistia.
The chiefs of Edom will be terrified, the leaders of Moab will be seized with
trembling, the people of Canaan will melt away; terror and dread will fall on
them." - Ex 15:14-16a (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The song looks ahead. News of the sea will travel, and nations Israel has not yet
met will hear about it.

Remarkably, this proved true. Forty years later, Rahab told Israel's spies in
Jericho that her city had heard how the LORD dried up the Red Sea, and that
everyone's courage had failed (Josh 2:10-11). The song was right, and it was
right decades in advance.

But look carefully at what happened with Rahab. The same news that terrified
Jericho brought her to faith. She said, "the LORD your God is God in heaven above
and on the earth below." She acted on it, and she is named in the family line of
Jesus (Matt 1:5) and among the heroes of faith (Heb 11:31).

So this passage is not simply about God's people being feared. It is about God's
reputation travelling, and about what different hearts do with the same report.

There is something here about our own witness. What God does in a life becomes
news. People hear. Some are unsettled by it and keep their distance. Others,
quietly, become curious and come closer.

We are not responsible for which. We are responsible for the report being true.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What does your life report about God to those watching?
2. Has news of God's work ever unsettled you before it drew you in?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, let the truth about You travel through my life. Use even what unsettles
people to draw them to Yourself. Amen.
